source.title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Applying Operations

teaching.hint: How many different rotation offsets and per-digit additions can repeated operations produce before they cycle?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Both operations are periodic. Repeated rotation reaches a bounded set of offsets; repeated addition reaches a bounded set of digit shifts. Odd versus even rotation distance determines whether additions can affect both index parities.
solution_outline.approach: Enumerate offsets reachable by repeated rotation. For each, enumerate the ten possible odd-position addition counts; when b is odd, independently enumerate ten possible even-position addition counts as well. Construct each reachable candidate and retain the lexical minimum.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Every enumerated candidate is reachable by a combination of allowed rotations and additions, and the enumeration covers every reachable rotation offset and allowed parity-class digit shift. The running best is the minimum candidate inspected.
solution_outline.correctness: Rotations generate offsets that are multiples of b modulo the even length, and additions generate multiples of a modulo ten. Even b preserves parity, leaving original even-position digits unchanged; odd b swaps parities, letting a rotate-add-rotate-back sequence shift either class independently. These combinations are closed under both operations and are reachable from the original, so they are exactly the orbit. Minimizing over them returns the required string.
solution_outline.complexity: O(100 n^2) time for at most n rotation states, at most 100 parity-shift combinations each, and O(n) construction/comparison; O(n) auxiliary space for candidates.
solution_outline.pitfall: Allowing even-index digit shifts when b is even can report a lexically smaller string that cannot be reached.

accepted_alternatives: Breadth-first search over strings generated by the two operations, with a visited set, also explores the finite reachable orbit; there are at most 100n states, each processed in O(n) time, using O(100n^2) stored characters.
common_wrong_turns: Assume one add then one rotation is enough
Shift original even positions when only even rotations are possible
Choose a local lexicographic improvement without exploring the reachable orbit
source_fidelity_notes: Long operation traces were omitted; 0-based odd indices, digit wraparound, right rotation, arbitrary repetitions, even length, bounds, and lexical objective were retained.
